ui_these_are_generic_examples_used_by_th: These are generic examples used by this app, not a claim that every project uses the same symbol. The symbols were created by Marc Sonne Dahl for this teaching reference.
ui_these_are_example_drawing_symbols_use: These are example drawing symbols. Use the legend supplied with the project to establish the meaning of each symbol. Channel counts, ratings, connections and supported functions must be checked against the drawing and the device documentation.
ui_a_tx_confirmation_is_a_local_link_lay: A TX confirmation is a local link-layer result, not an actuator-state report. The capture does not establish the full route or physical bus waveform.
ui_the_message_code_and_additional_infor: The message code and additional information belong to cEMI. TP1 parity, physical timing and check byte are not present here. Unrecognised services remain raw; no application decoding is inferred. Timestamps are recording timestamps, not measured wire timing.
ui_size_and_unused_compact_bits_narrow_t: Size and unused compact bits narrow the candidates; they do not identify the DPT. Reserved values and semantic constraints are checked only by implemented decoders. Variable-length and manufacturer-specific types may also exist.
ui_identifiers_names_and_format_codes_we: Identifiers, names and format codes were checked against the supplied standard overview. This is an edition-specific reference, not a claim to include every DPT in later editions. All 69 previously missing descriptions have been researched.
ui_entries_still_need_source_clarificati: entries still need source clarification; other inherited descriptions remain marked as unverified.
ui_a_dpt_tells_sender_and_receiver_how_t: A DPT tells sender and receiver how to interpret a value. Its main number identifies the format and encoding; the subtype specifies its meaning, range and unit. Matching size alone does not make two DPTs interchangeable. For standard group objects, configure the DPT in ETS: group-value telegrams do not carry its identifier.
ui_values_are_shown_most_significant_oct: Values are shown most-significant octet first; TP1 sends the bits within each octet least-significant bit first. Check the subtype’s reserved values, validity flags and application restrictions. Counter types are not arbitrary data containers, and overview format codes can omit padding shown in the detailed layout.
ui_a_character_b_boolean_bit_set_f_float: A: character · B: Boolean/bit set · F: float · N: enumeration · U: unsigned · V: signed two’s complement · r: reserved · Z8: standard status/command. Numeric suffixes are field widths in bits; A[n] is a character string.
ui_for_property_responses_and_lte_inform: For property responses and LTE information reports, Z8 is status: b0 OutOfService, b1 Fault, b2 Overridden, b3 InAlarm, b4 AlarmUnAck; b5–b7 must be zero. OutOfService cannot be combined with Fault or Overridden. Fault normally replaces the measurement with failure information (0 general, 1 open circuit, 2 short circuit); a supported override can make the substituted value valid despite Fault.
ui_for_property_writes_z8_is_a_command_e: For property writes, Z8 is a command enumeration: 0 NormalWrite, 1 Override, 2 Release, 3 SetOSV, 4 ResetOSV, 5 AlarmAck, 6 SetToDefault; 7–255 reserved. Main value is used for 0, 1 and 4 (4 may be ignored); it is irrelevant for 2, 3, 5 and 6. Supported commands/status flags depend on the datapoint; unsupported status flags are zero.
ui_these_z8_types_are_not_applicable_to_: These Z8 types are not applicable to ordinary shared-variable Group Objects: GroupValueWrite cannot distinguish a status report from a command. They therefore have no transfer button to this group-value Telegram Visualiser. Reference: §4.1.2, printed pages 107–110.
ui__the_encoder_below_uses_its_canonical: . The encoder below uses its canonical representation; rounding and equivalent float encodings can change the bytes.
ui_encoding_practice_only_this_parameter: Encoding practice only: this parameter, diagnostic or LTE structure is not offered as an ordinary group-value telegram.
ui_all_453_names_and_overview_formats_we: All 453 names and overview formats were cross-checked. Sizes were reconciled with the overview format; 24 further corrections were checked against subtype detail pages. Data-type labels were corrected for reviewed entries; other labels remain imported. Interactive widths are covered by tests. A verified identity is not a verified semantic layout.
ui_unit_transcribed_from_the_standard_s_: Unit transcribed from the standard’s F32 subtype table. Spelling follows the supplied edition; apparent editorial anomalies should be checked against KNX errata.
ui_no_change_recorded_in_the_supplied_ch: No change recorded in the supplied change log. The inherited range/layout text is not assumed to have been checked.
ui_follow_a_normal_group_telegram_from_1: Follow a normal group telegram from 1.1.252 to 15.1.255 through the devices shown below. The normal starting hop count (HC) is 6. A forwarding coupler or legacy line repeater receives HC > 0 and sends it onward with HC reduced by one. An incoming HC of 0 prevents another crossing; receivers on the reached segment can still accept the telegram.
ui_scope_ordinary_group_addressed_traffi: Scope: ordinary group-addressed traffic, matching receiver with C/W enabled, healthy TP links and no repetitions or ACK simulation. Each relevant group-address filter permits forwarding unless you select a rejection below. HC 7 has special non-decrementing behavior; it is outside this ordinary-traffic simulation, not an extra hop to use in planning.
ui_each_extension_connects_to_its_line_s: Each extension connects to its line’s main segment. This selected cross-area path has one repeater at each end and four line/backbone couplers: six crossings. That count belongs to this path; shorter paths use fewer. With HC 6, the final segment receives HC 0, with no forwarding budget left.
ui_three_legacy_repeaters_in_series_at_e: Three legacy repeaters in series at each end create ten crossings. This demonstrates the failure of this arrangement; it is not a permitted legacy repeater topology or a general ten-hop KNX rule. The trace stops at the first coupler that cannot forward.
ui_dashed_green_lines_show_the_example_b: Dashed green lines show the example bus connections. Directional arrows trace the selected telegram path; each HC label is the value carried into the next device.
ui_the_lr_devices_in_this_demonstration_: The LR devices in this demonstration are legacy TP1 repeaters: they extend a line without group-address filtering. A modern segment coupler connects subsegments within a logical line and supports filter tables, including ETS-managed individual-address filtering. Do not treat its behavior or permitted arrangement as identical to the legacy repeater example. The illustrated addresses do not define required segment boundaries.
ui_the_normal_traffic_hc_budget_and_filt: The normal-traffic HC budget and filtering are separate decisions. Reaching HC 0 on the destination segment is allowed; forwarding it through another coupler is not. A healthy cable and an adequate HC do not override a filter rejection.
ui_sources_knx_basic_tp_topology_section: Sources: KNX Basic, “TP Topology”, sections 8 and 14; KNX Advanced, “Couplers”, sections 2.3–2.4. This is a teaching trace, not a complete KNX network validator.
ui_two_area_couplers_across_the_top_line: Two area couplers across the top, line 1.1 on the left and line 15.1 on the right. Dashed green lines show TP bus connections. Arrows show only the selected path from 1.1.252 to 15.1.255. HC labels appear as the trace advances. Red dotted arrows mark the unreached remainder after a rejection.
ui_solid_arrow_traced_telegram_grey_dash: Solid arrow: traced telegram · grey dashed: pending · red dotted: not reached · outline: current event / rejection
ui_hc_hop_count_device_colours_identify_: HC = hop count. Device colours identify their functions, not reception status. The arrows trace one selected path; telegram propagation into other branches is not animated. Bus devices do not forward telegrams. Addresses are examples; power supplies are omitted.
ui_select_a_line_and_budget_its_main_seg: Select a line and budget its main segment. Each electrically separated subsegment needs its own calculation and supply. The line selector labels this working example; changing it keeps your entered budget. The address directory below is independent of this calculation.
ui_illustrative_values_not_product_speci: Illustrative values, not product specifications. Enter each product’s specified maximum KNX bus current. Count every connected coupler interface for electrical loading, even when its individual address belongs to another line. Use its actual current draw from this side, including 0 mA if documented.
ui_independent_checks_current_quantity_m: Independent checks: current = Σ(quantity × mA); interface load = 4 × TP1-64 + TP1-256 ≤ 256. Passing both is not a complete installation check: verify address allocation, cable length, voltage drop, supply/choke instructions and topology. No fixed 10 mA assumption and no network-wide current total. Supplies must not simply be paralleled to add their ratings.
ui_logical_bits_below_run_b7_b0_on_the_w: Logical bits below run b7 → b0. On the wire, data bits travel D0 → D7, preceded by Start and followed by even Parity and Stop.
ui_the_monitor_displays_logical_bytes_se: The monitor displays logical bytes, serial bits, field descriptions and an illustrative TP1 waveform. Generated frames remain available when switching pages.
ui_two_idle_bit_periods_separate_charact: Two idle bit periods separate characters; no extra gap is appended after the check character.
ui_1_1_10_asks_group_1_0_1_for_its_value: 1.1.10 asks group 1/0/1 for its value. Sensor 1.1.20 answers with 23.5 °C (DPT 9.001). These are separate telegrams; an application response is not a link-layer ACK.
ui_these_examples_generate_immediately_w: These examples generate immediately. Whether a response occurs depends on object configuration; no fixed response delay is implied.
ui_changes_apply_immediately_to_the_resp: Changes apply immediately to the response illustration. They do not change the generated telegram bytes. This is a selected teaching scenario, not a simulated receiver.
ui_communication_is_superimposed_on_the_: Communication is superimposed on the DC bus supply. A zero actively lowers the bus voltage; a one has no active pulse. Neither conductor is a protective-earth reference.
ui_the_active_pulse_is_followed_by_posit: The active pulse is followed by positive equalization and a return toward the resting voltage. The bus choke, integrated or separate, is essential. Actual shapes depend on the transmitter, cable and loading.
ui_the_tutor_overview_gives_21_32_v_dc_a: The Tutor overview gives 21–32 V DC, a 3–10 V drop and up to +13 V overshoot. These are separate from this example’s 29 / 22 / 36 V levels. The curve is not a tolerance envelope.
ui_arbitrary_bits_only_no_framing_valida: Arbitrary bits only. No framing validation, acknowledgement or telegram-cycle timing is implied. The generated byte cards remain unchanged.
ui_last_generated_telegram_all_intervals: Last generated telegram. All intervals share the same time scale; scroll horizontally to reach the response. Click a byte below to inspect its character.
ui_in_knx_a_group_object_for_example_a_s: In KNX, a group object (for example, a switching object in a push-button sensor) can be associated with multiple Group Addresses (GAs). However, a standard multicast telegram only has room for
ui_because_the_destination_field_only_ho: Because the destination field only holds one address, a sensor cannot natively transmit a single telegram to multiple Group Addresses at the same time. It will always transmit solely to its designated
ui__which_defaults_to_the_first_linked_a: , which defaults to the first linked address in ETS and can be changed explicitly. Here, the first checked address is used until it is unlinked.
ui_simple_dpt_1_001_switch_objects_the_s: Simple DPT 1.001 switch objects: the sensor’s Communication (C) and Transmit (T) flags are assumed enabled. Each receiver updates only when the destination GA is linked and its C and W flags allow the write. Other telegrams and link edits leave the lamp state unchanged.
ui_resides_only_on_the_first_group_addre: resides only on the first Group Address checked for Sensor 1. If you check both boxes, Sensor 1 links to both GAs in the matrix, but only one GA receives the (S) tag. This demonstrates why the actuator link logic depends on which Group Address the sensor actively outputs to.
ui_this_independent_access_scenario_does: This independent access scenario does not change the generated bytes. After the response stop bit: 50 bit periods for System, Alarm/urgent or a repeated telegram; 53 for an original High/normal or Low telegram. The 15-bit acknowledgement gap starts at the check character’s stop-bit end.
ui_course_comparison_for_a_9_character_s: Course comparison: for a 9-character switching frame with a 50-bit wait, Advanced counts 9 × 13 + 15 + 11 + 50 = 193 bits (20.07 ms using its rounded 0.104 ms/bit); this app counts only the eight internal 2-bit gaps, giving 191 bits (19.896 ms at 9600 bit/s). The app places the wait after the acknowledgement, as next-access eligibility.
ui_the_course_introduces_50_bits_for_sys: The course introduces 50 bits for System plus 3 bits for lower priorities. The fuller rule used here is in KNX TP1 v01.02.02 §2.3.2, Figure 41 (printed p. 36), and Annex B (p. 48): Alarm/urgent and repeated frames also qualify at 50 bits; only original High/normal and Low frames require 53.
ui_earliest_access_is_a_nominal_eligibil: Earliest access is a nominal eligibility boundary assuming a continuously idle bus, not a scheduled next telegram or retry. Contention, fairness delays and retry-specific waits are not simulated. Reference: KNX TP1 §2.3, Figures 38–41.
ui_for_simultaneous_group_acknowledgemen: For simultaneous group acknowledgements, the Tutor course gives BUSY → NAK → ACK priority. A group ACK cannot identify which individual receivers acknowledged. Negative or absent responses can cause repetitions; these are not included in the displayed frame and acknowledgement. Reference: Tutor §3.6.4.
ui_this_template_has_a_tp_backbone_15_tp: This template has a TP backbone, 15 TP main lines and 225 secondary lines. Each secondary line illustrates three segment couplers and four separately powered segments. Ordinary device positions are available slots, not installed devices. The former 59,687 total mixed incompatible quantities and has been removed.
ui_positions_255_15_256_225_256_61_695_s: Positions: 255 + 15 × 256 + 225 × 256 = 61,695. Supplies: 1 backbone + 15 main lines + 225 × 4 line segments = 916. Unaddressed supplies add no individual addresses. A supply with its own KNX diagnostic interface does need an address and must be budgeted as a bus device.
ui_a_coupler_has_one_individual_address_: A coupler has one individual address but a bus interface on each connected segment. For example, the 15 backbone-coupler interfaces also load the backbone, and the 15 line-coupler interfaces load each main line. Thus not every available address slot can be populated simultaneously on one TP segment. Electrical loading, PSU current, cable constraints and product specifications must all be checked separately.
ui_the_16_bit_address_field_contains_65_: The 16-bit address field contains 65,536 bit patterns; that is neither a count of installable devices nor this template’s capacity. Reserved positions and topology placement still apply. Sources: KNX Basic, “TP Topology”, sections 3–5 and 8; KNX Advanced, “Couplers”.
ui_segment_couplers_occupy_ordinary_devi: Segment couplers occupy ordinary device addresses on their line. Here .64, .128 and .192 are example allocations, not mandatory boundaries: a device’s address does not identify its physical segment. These couplers are included within the 256 address positions, never added on top. Each electrical segment has its own KNX supply with choke; the PSU badges show infrastructure, not addresses. No paired or redundant supplies are assumed.
ui_bus_voltage_between_red_and_black_lin: Bus voltage between red (+) and black (−). Linear voltage scale; 29 V resting, 7 V drop and +7 V equalization peak are illustrative.
ui_zero_35_microseconds_at_22_volts_then: Zero: 35 microseconds at 22 volts, then equalization from 36 toward 29 volts. One: passive at 29 volts. Each bit lasts 104.167 microseconds.
ui_references_knx_tutor_course_serial_da: References: KNX Tutor course, Serial Data Transmission §§3.7.1–3.7.4, Figures 9–11; KNX Basic course, System overview §§10–13.2. Timing: KNX TP1 §2.3 and Annex B; nominal character and access intervals, without physical tolerances. Analogue amplitudes and decay are illustrative.
ui_line_coupler_area_coupler_line_repeat: Line coupler / area coupler / line repeater
ui_supplies_the_knx_tp_bus_with_dc_power: Supplies the KNX TP bus with DC power through an integrated choke. The choke allows communication signals to remain on the bus. Choose the supply rating to suit the connected devices and segment design.
ui_controls_the_brightness_of_compatible: Controls the brightness of compatible lighting in response to KNX commands. The supported load type, dimming method and number of channels depend on the actuator.
ui_controls_up_down_movement_of_compatib: Controls up/down movement of compatible blind or shutter motors. Depending on the device and configuration, it can also control position and slat angle.
ui_a_manual_input_device_that_sends_conf: A manual input device that sends configured KNX commands when operated, for example switching, dimming, blind movement or scene recall. Its function is assigned during configuration.
ui_a_shared_drawing_symbol_for_three_dis: A shared drawing symbol for three distinct roles. A line coupler connects a line to its main line; an area coupler connects a main line to the backbone. A TP line repeater extends a line across segments. State the actual role in the project legend: coupling and repeating follow different forwarding rules.
ui_connects_a_computer_to_the_knx_bus_vi: Connects a computer to the KNX bus via USB, for example for commissioning and diagnostics with ETS. It provides access to the bus; it does not replace a bus power supply.
ui_provides_access_to_knx_over_an_ip_net: Provides access to KNX over an IP network. An IP interface typically provides KNXnet/IP tunnelling for a client such as ETS. An IP router also supports KNXnet/IP routing between KNX lines over IP. Identify the actual device role in the project legend.
ui_processes_knx_values_using_configured: Processes KNX values using configured logic, conditions, timers or calculations, then sends resulting commands or values. Available functions depend on the controller and its application.
ui_exchanges_configured_commands_and_sta: Exchanges configured commands and status information between KNX and another system. Identify the other system and the supported functions in the project legend and device documentation.
ui_displays_knx_values_and_status_inform: Displays KNX values and status information. An interactive screen can also send commands for functions such as lighting, shading or room control; an information-only display may provide no controls.
ui_detects_infrared_changes_for_function: Detects infrared changes for functions such as motion or presence detection and sends the configured KNX information. Coverage, sensitivity and occupancy-related functions depend on the sensor and its installation.
ui_switches_connected_electrical_loads_o: Switches connected electrical loads on or off in response to KNX commands. The number of channels, contact ratings and supported load types depend on the actuator.
ui_measures_or_detects_a_physical_condit: Measures or detects a physical condition and makes the value or state available to KNX, for example temperature, brightness or a contact state. Specify the measured quantity in the project legend.
ui_repeaters_connected_to_the_main_segme: Repeaters connected to the main segment
ui_select_generate_telegram_on_the_teleg: Select Generate Telegram on the Telegram page to display a frame.
ui_previous_telegram_regenerate_to_apply: Previous telegram — regenerate to apply edited settings.
ui_generated_telegram_matches_the_curren: Generated telegram matches the current settings.
ui_generate_a_telegram_to_calculate_timi: Generate a telegram to calculate timing.
ui_ack_confirms_link_layer_reception_it_: ACK confirms link-layer reception. It does not prove that an actuator performed an action or that an application response will follow.
ui_nak_reports_a_reception_error_a_sende: NAK reports a reception error. A sender can repeat the telegram according to its retry behaviour.
ui_busy_reports_that_the_receiving_link_: BUSY reports that the receiving link layer cannot process the telegram because its buffers are full. Retry handling is device-dependent.
ui_the_selected_demonstration_shows_no_a: The selected demonstration shows no acknowledgement and a silent nominal response slot. This is not evidence of silence in an imported capture, a specified timeout or a complete failed transaction. Retry timing is not calculated.
ui_combine_with_the_next_octet_s_two_mos: Combine with the next octet’s two most significant bits.
ui_small_value_or_zero_for_a_read__31526: Small value, or zero for a read.
ui_part_of_the_selected_dpt_payload_dpt_: Part of the selected DPT payload. DPT identifiers are not carried in the telegram.
ui_not_xor_of_preceding_octets_xor_of_th: NOT-XOR of preceding octets; XOR of the whole frame is FF.
ui_rounded_to_the_nearest_1_255_of_full_: Rounded to the nearest 1/255 of full scale.
ui_knx_16_bit_floating_point_the_encoded: KNX 16-bit floating point; the encoded value may be rounded.
ui_scene_numbers_are_displayed_with_a_1_: Scene numbers are displayed with a +1 offset. Bit 6 is reserved and remains zero.
locale.partial: English reference text is shown where a Danish translation is not yet available.
route.source: Source sends a group telegram with HC {{hc}}.
route.receiver: Telegram present on this segment with HC {{hc}}. End devices do not forward it; a linked receiver may accept it even at HC 0.
route.zero: Not forwarded: incoming HC is 0. Devices on the incoming segment can still receive it.
route.filter: Not forwarded: destination group address is absent from this coupler’s filter table.
route.repeater: Repeater has no group-address filter; forwarded with HC {{before}} → {{after}}.
route.forward: Group-address filter permits this route; forwarded with HC {{before}} → {{after}}.
